The same failures occur locally when pre-commit runs outside the production environment. Fix the environment provisioning or the guardrail loader so it can run without importing every third-party dependency, or mark guardrail checks as environment-dependent and run them in a dedicated step rather than in the pre-commit/lint path.
notes:

title: Follow-up research: client-side/remote plugin model
description: Research only - no code changes, no merges. The prior report (handoffs/plugin-architecture-research-2026-08-28-report.md) researched in-process plugin packaging (Candidates A/B/C). Brad rejected that model. Redo the research for a client-side/remote plugin model: plugins run on the end user's own machine (their compute, their RAM) and connect back to Core (hosted on Semptify's server) over an API, not via in-process Python imports. Research questions: (1) What does Core's public API surface need to expose for a remote plugin to authenticate and exchange data (auth token pattern, rate limiting, versioned endpoints)? (2) How does a client-side plugin authenticate, given storage-as-identity is OAuth to the tenant's own cloud - does the plugin get its own token, or use the tenant's existing session? (3) What would download-and-install locally packaging look like (desktop app? browser extension? local script + config file)? (4) What precedent exists for this pattern (Photoshop/Ableton-style plugin ecosystems for a web-service-backed tool) - name directly comparable open-source or documented examples. (5) Any conflict with existing locks (storage-as-identity, no PII on Semptify servers, Python 3.11.9 mandate where applicable)? Deliverable: handoffs/plugin-architecture-clientside-research-2026-08-28-report.md, same format as prior report (candidates + pros/cons + decision points Brad can answer in one word/tap).
notes:
From planning session 2026-08-28 (Brad + Claude). Supersedes in-process research in plugin-architecture-research-2026-08-28-report.md. Context: Core now includes identity+storage-auth, the Flagship experience (bundled/hosted, no plugin install for tenant in crisis), and the plugin directory/gateway (marketplace page + API surface). Plugin execution model is client-side, not in-process. Plugin grouping/application deferred to later session.
[2026-08-29 02:54 UTC - claude] Research complete. Report covers: (1) Core API surface needs (versioned /api/v1/, plugin token issuance, rate limiting, CORS, plugin directory endpoint, structured JSON); (2) Plugin auth via delegated session token (Option A recommended -- plugin gets scoped bearer token from Core, Core mediates all storage, storage-as-identity preserved); (3) Three packaging candidates: D=browser extension, E=desktop app (Electron/Tauri), F=local script; (4) Precedents: Figma plugins (server-mediated OAuth, sandboxed JS), VS Code extensions (AuthenticationProvider API, delegated token), Adobe UXP (WebSocket bridge), Hermes Desktop (SDK import, file-drop), Plumbus (bearer token store, typed client); (5) No conflicts with existing locks. 5 decision points for Brad.
